memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Take the garments and dress Aaron with the tunic, the robe of the ephod, the ephod itself and the breastpiece. Fasten the ephod on him by its skillfully woven waistband. Put the turban on his head and attach the sacred emblem to the turban." - Exodus 29:5-6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice who does the dressing. Moses puts the garments on Aaron. Aaron does not dress himself, does not fasten his own ephod, does not place the turban on his own head. He stands still and receives. Every piece of his priestly identity is placed on him by someone else.

There is deep humility in that. The high priest of Israel began his ministry passively, being clothed rather than clothing himself. It was a physical enactment of grace — everything he needed for his office was given to him, not generated by him.

This is precisely our position before God. Paul writes that we have clothed ourselves with Christ (Gal 3:27), and Isaiah rejoiced that God had arrayed him in a robe of righteousness (Isa 61:10). The righteousness we stand in is not woven by our own effort. It is placed on us. When you are tempted to feel that your standing with God depends on your performance, remember Aaron standing still while Moses dressed him. Receive what has been given. You did not make this robe, and you cannot improve on it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Am I trying to weave my own righteousness rather than receiving Christ's?
What would change if I truly rested in being clothed rather than self-made?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I did not weave my own righteousness — You clothed me in Christ. Help me stop striving to earn what You have freely placed on me, and rest in Your gift. Amen.
